name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or another Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model. Settle occurred facts, summaries, simulations, calculation ownership, persistence, and correction before capability discovery. Only two or more unresolved, mutually incompatible choices that change an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow form a product business ambiguity; block only the smallest affected modeling slice. Missing optional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms are not product blockers. Contract discovery and reversible technical defaults are not substitutes for business facts.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect routes, screens, typed API contracts, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. This Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes `frontend/**`, frontend component contracts, or Runtime Client SDK assets. Shared Application Delivery still publishes the Runtime Client SDK for an independent frontend Skill; this Builder Skill never fetches, copies, installs, generates, validates, or takes ownership of it. Route each mismatch to the owner proved by the explicit requirement, published Runtime contract, typed frontend API, Mock/tests, and real behavior. A frontend- or Mock-owned mismatch is a finding for owner `frontend`, never a backend workaround or frontend edit.

## Route exactly once

Choose one route before loading supporting resources. Do not combine the routes.

### Whole-project development

For every normal requirements, build, repair, integration, acceptance, or whole-project continuation batch, read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) **completely before starting** and use it as the only execution workflow. One Host/Agent session and TODO own requirements → model → apply → implementation → verify → package → Runtime → canary → acceptance, including recoverable repair rounds. Follow every applicable routed reference. A light batch may omit only TODO sections allowed by the guide, never guide loading or an applicable authority.

The routing map below is a reachability contract, not permission to read only selected guide sections:

| Moved entrypoint section / contract | Whole-project authority |
| --- | --- |
| workflow, routing, and batch scale | [whole-project workflow](references/development-guide.md#whole-project-workflow) |
| loaded Skill, CLI identity, and normal command surface | [CLI identity and canonical command map](references/development-guide.md#cli-identity-and-canonical-command-map) |
| complete TODO, Gate first-execution receipts, and session ownership | [session TODO and Gate receipts](references/development-guide.md#session-todo-and-gate-receipts) |
| project ownership and frontend finding routing | [project and frontend boundaries](references/development-guide.md#project-and-frontend-boundaries) |
| requirements extraction and critical ambiguity | [requirements to domain facts](references/development-guide.md#requirements-to-domain-facts) |
| domain truth, settlement, list Report, and technical prevention Gates | [domain truth design](references/development-guide.md#domain-truth-design) |
| capability reconciliation and metadata modeling | [model and capability mapping](references/development-guide.md#model-and-capability-mapping) |
| declarative authoring and the only release command | [model apply is the only release](references/development-guide.md#model-apply-is-the-only-release) |
| bounded installed-batch Action context | [source prepare implementation packet](references/development-guide.md#source-prepare-implementation-packet) |
| valid check, source finalize, focused tests, and exact receipts | [project check to finalize to tests](references/development-guide.md#project-check-to-finalize-to-tests) |
| semantic journey binding and highest-risk canary | [semantic execution and canary](references/development-guide.md#semantic-execution-and-canary) |
| managed Runtime and exact-denominator acceptance | [Runtime and acceptance](references/development-guide.md#runtime-and-acceptance) |
| evidence ceiling and terminal states | [done terminal policy](references/development-guide.md#done-terminal-policy) |
| initial credential and acceptance-identity safety | [system seed login](references/development-guide.md#system-seed-login) |

### Explicit source-finalization continuation

Use this route only when the caller explicitly requests `source-finalization-continuation`, accepts and freezes upstream requirements/modeling, confirms the current source-finalization checkpoint remains valid, and limits scope exactly to:

```text
valid Actions project check → source finalize → module-focused Go test
```

Run the loaded Skill's resolver once with an explicit project-relative focused package:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --profile source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

Before resolving or resuming this continuation, prove the original Host/Agent turn has actually ended. An outer exec session reporting `Unknown process id`, missing its timing trailer, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence and must never trigger a concurrent Agent against the same session. The returned `continuation` envelope atomically owns this session's three-Gate TODO, synchronized Gate IDs, current checkpoint identity, and exact `run_recipes`. Execute those recipes in order and use no other workflow. Do **not** read `references/development-guide.md`, `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`, or any whole-project reference for this profile.

This route is caller authorization, never inferred from project state. Missing, stale, unsafe, or ambiguous session/checkpoint/CLI identity, a package outside the project, a missing focused package, or a conflicting/partial session TODO fails closed. Do not repair such a conflict by deleting or rewriting managed state. The compact route does not bypass the Host's complete loading of this `SKILL.md` and does not change whole-project behavior.

### Explicit post-apply source-finalization continuation

Use this distinct compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` after a fresh successful `model apply` materialization whose source finalization failed solely on generated project-owned Action placeholders, and the caller has completed those Action sources. It does not accept or alter the already-current `source-finalization-continuation` route.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile post-apply-source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

The resolver validates the current signed backend materialization and its exact machine failure receipt before creating state. That receipt must contain only the structured `project.source_placeholder_remains` diagnostics for Action source in the `backend_technical_contract` check; every independent preflight check must have passed, and only the dependent composition check may be skipped. The current source must be a placeholder-free, finalization-ready evolution of that receipt in which only project-owned `backend/actions/**` paths changed. Runtime Client SDK and frontend materialization receipts are never accepted.

On success the resolver atomically owns one TODO, Gate state, and profile with exactly three ordered one-shot recipes:

```text
project check --scope actions → project source finalize → focused Go test
```

Execute only the returned `run_recipes`. Do not edit, add, reorder, duplicate, reopen, attach evidence to, or invoke the underlying product commands outside the profile runner. Partial state, symlinks, traversal or unbounded package paths, changed materialization/failure/source/CLI identities, a forged receipt, any non-placeholder failure, terminal failure, or a different/extra Gate fails closed with no replacement TODO. A completed terminal profile returns no recipes and never reopens. Do **not** read the whole-project guide, TODO template, or another whole-project reference for this profile.

### Explicit project verification continuation

Use this compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-verification-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. It is independent from package continuation. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-verification-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint validates the current backend-only materialization, source finalization and identity, Runtime manifest, and backend Application Delivery binding. Python consumes that checkpoint and atomically owns any required one-Gate TODO/state/profile. If verification is already current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise execute the sole returned machine-owned `project verify --json` recipe exactly once. Never supply a label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or binding. Partial/conflicting/unsafe state, stale profile identity, receipt tampering, an extra or reordered Gate, a repeated terminal command, or a changed pre-execution checkpoint fails closed without replacement.

### Explicit project package continuation

Use this separate compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-package-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-package-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint requires the current V6 verification plus the same current backend binding/materialization/finalization/source/Runtime identity closure. If the package receipt is current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise it atomically owns one machine Gate and returns only the fixed `project package --json` recipe. Execute it exactly once; never author its label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or bindings. The same partial, conflict, symlink/traversal, stale/tamper, extra/reordered Gate, terminal-repeat, and pre-execution-change cases fail closed without overwriting state or accepting an older receipt.

### Explicit Runtime process continuation

Use this compact route when the caller asks only to recover the already-packaged managed Runtime start/status boundary. Use the current Host session ID for this fresh compact continuation; do not create or reuse a whole-project TODO for that session. It does not require loading the whole-project guide, verification references, TODO template, verification authorities, or Gate runner source. Resolve the machine-owned profile once:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile runtime-process-continuation \
  --runtime-address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>
```

When the session has no TODO, Gate state, or Runtime profile, the resolver atomically creates its canonical two-Gate minimal TODO, synchronized state, and profile. It owns the fixed labels, `runtime_start` → `runtime_status` kinds, Gate IDs, exact argv, source/Runtime/cohort bindings, current packaged bundle, packaged CLI, numeric loopback address, and all pinned identities. The tool guarantees that the actual listener is the requested loopback and records its proof; the Agent adds no bind command or listener check. Stdout is only the compact envelope with the remaining `run_recipes`; execute them in order. Do not supply or author a TODO, label, marker, Gate ID, bundle, command argv, or identity binding yourself. Re-resolve after start to obtain only the status recipe when recovering from compaction. A partial session, non-profile-owned TODO, symlink, extra/reordered/forged Gate, changed address/package/source/CLI identity, stale state, terminal failure, or conflict fails closed without deleting or overwriting caller state; a terminal Gate never reopens.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Every Builder command, resolver, Gate runner, template, and reference must come from that same root. The package has one executable: `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Never discover it through `PATH`, substitute another installed Skill's binary, call Domainry Plane directly, or invent a neighboring command.

For whole-project work, the guide requires the default resolver once at task start and binds `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Host session ID, TODO, compact resume packet, one-time authoring context, and package identity to its result. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. For the explicit continuation, the compact resolver call above supplies and validates the same package CLI identity without loading whole-project context.

## Universal safety and evidence invariants

- Treat Runtime-owned identifiers, hierarchy values, principal claims, cursors, and other canonical representations as opaque. Resolve them through the published typed client, `GET /identity/principal-context`, a formal seed/admin path, or a persisted Runtime result and carry them unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them. A missing formal source blocks the affected journey.
- Keep project-owned authoring in `backend/model/*.json`, referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`, project-owned backend source/tests, and the current session's `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md`. Never hand-edit generated source, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned `.domainry/**` delivery state. Never create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that ignores its generated capabilities.
- `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. Repair model/input failures and rerun it through a new round-specific Gate in the same session TODO; never reopen a terminal Gate, split release steps, bypass review, or treat `--product-surfaces` as frontend authorization.
- Run each check, finalize, and focused test through its own Gate on first execution. The runner serializes the Gate across processes; a passed or failed receipt makes only that Gate terminal. `checkpoint`, `status`, and `--require-complete` are recovery evidence, not task-exit instructions. After repair, add a round-specific Gate to the same TODO, sync, rerun invalidated checks, and continue in the same Host/Agent session. Never rerun a terminal Gate or reuse another receipt.
- Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey to its requirement, formal actor/session/principal, canonical context and identifiers, isolated setup, command/read surfaces, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict and unchanged-state oracle, durable effect, and dependencies. Do not create a second plan. Scope-sensitive journeys use same-record contrasts through real Runtime sessions; arbitrary errors, empty results, and residue from another case do not prove success. For unchanged/replay record hashes, use `runtimeRecordDurableSnapshot` (or copied-harness `durable_record_snapshot`), never the whole HTTP response body.
- When a settled requirement explicitly names an initial/default field value, add one TODO checkpoint that records the requirement evidence, exact Object-field JSON Pointer, concrete `default_value`, and its matching option/state entry. Close it only after the pointer exists in the applied model and validation proves membership; never leave the behavior only in acceptance prose or infer a default from silence. The authoritative mapping and applied example are in [CRUD and state machine](references/capabilities/crud-and-state-machine.md).
- After finalization and focused tests pass, run the highest-risk semantic canary before broad Runtime integration. Failure makes dependents temporarily ineligible, never ends the task: repair its owner, add repair Gates to the same TODO, rerun invalidated checks, and continue without shrinking the model or denominator.
- Model validation, apply, source checks, verify, package, Runtime start/health, canary, and acceptance failures use the same bounded diagnose → owner repair → rerun loop. Keep all quality, safety, ownership, and denominator Gates; no compatibility layer, fallback, weaker oracle, excluded case, or reduced denominator. Stop only with exhausted evidence of unavailable required service/permission/credential, unresolvable result-changing ambiguity, data/security risk, or contradictory contracts.
- Never claim above current evidence. Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Completion requires the applicable evidence Gate, an empty finding inventory, the guide's terminal policy, and the TODO consistency check; unresolved product prerequisites are implementation/Foundation defects, not cosmetic limitations.

Record the attempted recovery paths and their evidence. Otherwise remain in the same Host/Agent session and TODO, repair, rerun, and continue. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. # Verification evidence levels

Use this ladder for every verify Gate and final claim. Each level includes the lower levels, but an artifact reaches a level only when its current proof exists and is bound to the current source/model/Runtime identity.

## Ladder

- `L0_declared`: the capability exists in requirements, model metadata, or source. This proves intent only.
- `L1_delivery_verified`: source finalization is current; format, lint, vet, tests, `project verify`, and packaging pass. This proves structural/release closure, not behavior.
- `L2_api_verified`: the operation executes through the real managed Runtime with a real session and its durable result is read back through the typed API or database. A denied/error/conflict case proves unchanged durable state; an idempotency case proves one effect after replay.
- `L3_scenario_verified`: every in-scope backend acceptance journey executes end to end on real Runtime data across its complete role/case matrix. Each permission boundary includes allow and deny probes; each data-scope rule uses differentiated identities and records; every mutation includes persistence evidence; Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, and outbox claims include their terminal observable effect.
- `L4_browser_verified`: **outside this Skill's acceptance scope.** The level number is reserved so the ladder stays stable, but browser-layer UI verification is never required, claimed, or a completion precondition here; backend delivery acceptance stops at L3/L5.
- `L5_restart_verified`: the critical L3 journey subset and sessions remain correct after a managed Runtime restart, with durable state read back and the critical cases rerun.

## Claim rules

- Never call L0/L1 output `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done`; say `declared` or `delivery_verified`.
- Never infer L2/L3 from a test name, source inspection, metadata checklist, `project verify`, package receipt, Runtime health, HTTP 2xx alone, TODO prose, or TODO checker success.
- Never count a click, toast, queued job, emitted event, waiting Workflow, metadata-only import/export record, or local state change as the terminal business effect.
- Report skipped checks as skipped. Do not fold them into a higher level.
- Report coverage only with its exact include scope. A subset percentage is not whole-project coverage.
- Treat missing, empty, partial, stale, unbound, contradictory, or hand-written summary evidence as non-passing.

## L3 evidence requirements

For every accepted operation/case row, bind project-local evidence to the current full-stack source digest and Runtime delivery identity. Record the operation, actor/role, case, request/response or execution identity, expected owner, permission and data scope, persistence probe, before/after state digest, audit/receipt identity when applicable, and result.

For non-`none` data scope, provide at least two distinguishable owners and two scope groups when the rule separates them, plus records inside and outside the actor's allowed scope. A single actor, team, owner, or record cannot prove a scope boundary.

For mutations:

- success requires different before/after state and a successful read-back;
- denied, validation, and conflict cases require identical before/after state;
- idempotent replay requires the replay state to equal the first successful after-state;
- restart persistence requires the post-restart state to equal the accepted pre-restart state.

## Minimum terminal level

Whole-project and Runtime-integrated backend completion require current L3 for every in-scope journey and L5 for every critical journey marked restart-sensitive. A light existing-project increment may reference prior current evidence for unchanged operations, but every changed operation and affected regression boundary must reach the same required level. Completion in this Skill is backend acceptance: L3 for every in-scope journey plus L5 for restart-sensitive ones; L4 browser evidence is never required. An observation has `kind`, project-relative `artifact`, `artifact_sha256`, and only for `persistence_snapshot` the required `before_sha256`/`after_sha256` plus replay SHA when applicable. Each artifact is strict JSON `domainry-backend-acceptance-artifact-v1` and binds its kind, case, operation, Runtime identity, producer source receipt, capture owner, and typed facts. Accepted kinds are `http_exchange`, `persistence_snapshot`, `idempotency_receipt`, `sse_transcript`, `durable_refetch`, `runtime_restart`, `worker_terminal`, `differentiated_scope_data`, `transaction_trace`, `pagination_trace`, `query_profile`, `audit_correlation`, `security_posture`, and `provider_receipt`. Pagination facts bind stable sort/tie-breaker and cursor strategy; offset fencing additionally requires the bound source version and observed stale-cursor rejection. Provider receipts bind the denominator's exact connector, connection, provider, operation; a durable provider or notification audit also requires its outbox reference. A correctly hashed arbitrary text file or a typed artifact whose endpoint, actor, outcome, transaction counts, page facts, process/database identity, differentiated data scope, or provider terminal state contradicts the denominator is rejected. The harness must preserve secrets safely, but redaction cannot remove facts needed to prove the case.

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The check reruns model derivation, resolves the live managed Runtime cohort, verifies every raw artifact, and requires exact set equality with the denominator. Missing, orphan, duplicate, failed, stale, unbound, unknown-kind, artifactless, or `self_reported` coverage fails. A percentage, prose claim, Mock transcript, or evidence from another Runtime can never satisfy it.

### Incremental re-recording after a model evolution

The denominator's `artifact_manifest` digests each operation's dependency closure, so an evolution no longer forces a blind full re-record: evidence recorded against an archived earlier generation stays binding when a complete hash proof chain shows nothing its case depends on changed. After any evolution, with the new denominator prepared, first run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The report (contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-stale-report-v1`) classifies every case as `current` (evidence still binds), `stale` (with reason), `missing`, or `declared_gap`, plus counts. Re-record ONLY the `stale` + `missing` subset. For the runner's mechanical families, re-run `project acceptance run --cases standard` on the same results file: it applies the same per-case carry-forward proof, keeps every `current` result (report field `carried_forward`), rebinds the file to the new denominator, and re-executes only what it dropped. For the remaining stale business-assertion cases, re-record through the harness core's stale-list resume — `stale_case_ids(<stale-report>)` plus `Harness(..., stale_report=...)` and `pending_cases(...)` — which rewrites only the affected result entries (evidence file paths are reused) instead of rebuilding the results file. Then run `acceptance check` as usual: a receipt with non-zero `carried_forward_cases` is a normal, complete result — carried-forward coverage is hash-proven, never a gap and never `self_reported`.

Carry-forward pays only when the repair converges on attributable model items (actions, workflows, reports, export controls, scheduled jobs, agent tasks — plus a report's own `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`). Any other project source change — handler code, config, anything else under `backend/**` — and any shared-collection change (objects, roles, workspaces, automation rules, seeds, ...) shifts the shared digest and makes every case stale; prefer model-item-level fixes and keep every working file out of `backend/**` (harness location discipline above).

Finish the complete verification round before repair. Preserve every first failure and continue safe checks to collect the full finding inventory. Then return findings to `requirements`, `model`, or `apply`, repair them together, create new round-specific Gates in the same session TODO for every invalidated command, and continue through Runtime, canary, and acceptance; a terminal Gate and its first receipt are never overwritten or rerun. This loop is bounded per round by the reachable inventory, one owner-grouped repair batch, and the affected checks, but repeats in this Agent session while an evidence-supported repair remains.

The CLI makes this concrete for local structural checks. A failed metadata checklist writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/checklist-failed.json`; a failed source finalization writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/finalization-failed.json`; a failed `project verify` writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/verification-failed.json`. Each check is `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped_dependency`. Safe independent checks run in the same round even when a sibling fails; dependency-bound checks are skipped explicitly. Treat every `failed` row as one repair inventory and never treat `skipped_dependency` as a pass. These receipts remain L1 structural evidence only.

Run and bind evidence for:

- protected source boundary (`frontend/**` untouched under every recorded frontend mutation scope — no frontend typecheck/test/build set exists in this Skill because it never changes frontend source), and current source finalization;
- backend format, lint, vet, focused tests, full tests, verification, and package receipts;
- exact Runtime delivery/manifest identity and healthy managed Runtime;
- real non-human acceptance sessions and differentiated seed data;
- the complete operation x role x required-case inventory;
- the current acceptance denominator and its passing exact-set check receipt;
- allowed and denied authorization, application-layer data scope, sensitive fields, durable effects, conflicts, errors, and idempotency;
- Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, outbox, and external-effect terminal outcomes;
- persistence read-back and critical-case restart persistence;
- cleanup of temporary records, processes, ports, and databases.

Acceptance in this Skill verifies backend logic end-to-end — real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior. Browser-layer UI verification is outside its acceptance scope and is never a completion precondition.

The evidence Gate must bind evidence content plus applicable source, model/Blueprint, and Runtime identities. A later identity or artifact-content change makes the Gate stale. Re-run commands or regenerate artifacts; never reattach unchanged prose.

Evidence rules — tool-produced content only: every evidence file's content must be produced by a command, script, or platform tool and carry what makes it reproducible (the recorded command line, or its source plus sha256). The model never hand-transcribes, excerpts, or re-arranges content into an evidence file. In the TODO, an `Evidence:` line carries only the gate ID and path pointers; inlining more than one line of content there is prohibited.

## Failure classification

- Missing credentials, acceptance identities, differentiated data, explicit Runtime configuration, routes, permissions, sessions, Runtime health, or persistence is normally an implementation/Foundation defect. Return it to its owner and repair it in the same session; it becomes an external blocker only when every authorized provisioning/recovery path remains unavailable with recorded evidence.
- `verification_blocked` is allowed only when implementation is complete and every authorized execution mechanism for a required check remains unavailable after all recovery paths, or when continuing would risk data corruption/security, a result-changing business ambiguity has no safe authority, or governing contracts are objectively contradictory. Name the blocked checks, recovery attempts, project-local/external evidence, and highest reached level.
- Missing, partial, skipped, failed, stale, unbound, contradictory, or insufficient behavior evidence from an ordinary round is a repair finding, not a blocker, task exit, or intentional prototype. It can become terminal `acceptance_failed` only after every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair has been exhausted and the same frozen contract still fails.
- A non-blocking limitation may be reported only when it is outside the frozen scope and does not weaken an in-scope claim.

## Terminal states

This terminal verification sequence applies to `Execution scope: implementation`. A `requirements_only` batch may move directly from closed requirements/domain-truth Gates to `done`; that state proves only the accepted requirements artifact, reports no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim, and must not imply Runtime or UI verification.

Record exactly one state:

- `done`: every in-scope Gate has current bound evidence at the required level, the acceptance matrix is complete, the finding inventory is empty, and no requirement is hidden, downgraded, or deferred.
- `acceptance_failed`: after the same-session repair loop exhausts every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair, implementation or evidence still fails the frozen acceptance contract. A first or ordinary failed acceptance round never qualifies.
- `verification_blocked`: implementation is complete but a required check cannot execute because no authorized execution capability exists.

Only `done` permits a whole-batch completion claim. Other states report per-capability results and the highest evidence level without upward summarization. Neither state is a shortcut around diagnosis: do not record it merely because validate/apply/verify/package/Runtime/canary/acceptance returned non-zero, and do not move a recoverable repair to user wait or another Host/Agent session.

Before completion, keep `Current stage: verify`, require the evidence Gate's `verify` status to pass, and run the TODO checker with `--expected-stage verify`. Change the stage to `done` only after terminal policy permits it; then require the Gate's `done` status and run the TODO checker again immediately before the final response.

The final summary states terminal state, implemented scope, frontend mutation scope, current delivery identity, tests/builds, Runtime result, highest evidence level, restart result, and open limitations. Never imply L4 browser evidence — it is outside this Skill's acceptance scope.

# Production technical gates

Read this file completely before model authoring, source implementation, Runtime integration, or terminal verification. These gates cover the backend and its published Runtime contract boundary. They do not assess page layout or visual quality.

## Gate semantics

A gate is `applicable`, `not_applicable`, or `failed`; it is never silently skipped. `not_applicable` requires a machine-derived reason tied to the current model and capability inventory. An applicable gate passes only with both its declared static proof and its real Runtime proof. Static validation can reject a structurally unsafe candidate, but cannot prove transaction rollback, cross-request idempotency, concurrent correctness, query boundedness, tenant isolation, worker recovery, SSE resume, or external-provider terminal effects.

The complete denominator contains the 32 gate families below. A project may have multiple cases for one family. The acceptance denominator must bind every case to the current model, Blueprint, CLI-compiled capability disclosure, generated source, packaged Runtime binary, and database cohort identity. Any bound identity change makes the evidence stale. (Isolation is proven behaviorally and database-agnostically per G14; no engine-specific security posture is bound or required.)

Evidence may redact secrets and personal data, but must retain the route or operation, actor/role, workspace, request/idempotency/correlation identity, status or stable error code, state transition, cursor or job identity, and durable before/after digests needed to prove the case. A prose claim, test name, arbitrary file, 2xx response, `queued`, `waiting`, or self-reported percentage is not evidence.

## A. Contract and delivery closure

### G01 Requirement-to-operation closure

- Applies when any executable requirement exists.
- Model/static: every requirement behavior resolves to its owning resource, typed operation, allowed and denied actor, data scope, fixture, expected terminal effect and acceptance case. Every executable resource has the inverse link back to a requirement and at least one operation/case.
- Runtime: exercise each changed operation and reference current prior evidence only for unchanged operations.
- Blocks: orphan requirements/resources, a single generic case used to cover several distinct operations, or model inventory omitted from the denominator.

### G02 Capability disclosure parity

- Applies to every Business/Portal endpoint selected by the project.
- Model/static: route policy, OpenAPI operation/schema, Runtime Domain API, Runtime Client method, owner, permission, scope, idempotency and stream semantics are an exact set. Static status is named `contract_ready`; it must not imply configured or scenario-verified behavior.
- Runtime: prove the selected operation is enabled and executable in the current delivery; provider-backed capabilities also require provider verification.
- Blocks: undocumented routes, catalog-only routes reported as scenario ready, generic request fallback presented as a typed client implementation, or stale capability hashes.

### G03 Skill, source, documentation and binary parity

- Applies to every release of this Skill.
- Model/static: Skill command examples, Go dispatcher, repository binary, packaged binary, supported command list, version, capability names and contract hashes match. Every fenced/inline `Correct`, `minimal`, and pattern example is machine parsed and validated.
- Runtime: packaged binary, not only the Go `run()` function, executes version/help and mandatory command smoke tests.
- Blocks: a documented command absent from the shipped binary, contradictory capability claims, stale examples, or installed-package evidence used for a different source tree.

### G04 One frontend intent to one Runtime command

- Applies to every user intent that changes business state.
- Model/static: the call-site inventory maps one intent to exactly one Runtime Action/command entrypoint. The Action payload carries all data needed to complete the intent; project BFFs, raw HTTP and client-side write orchestration are forbidden.
- Runtime: one interaction produces one governed request identity and one terminal receipt. Internal typed capability calls may be multiple, but remain inside the single Runtime-owned work unit.
- Blocks: open-table/open-shift/payment/submit flows implemented as sequential create/update calls, client rollback, a second repair call, or refetch presented as another business command.

## B. Command correctness and consistency

### G05 Single command boundary

- Applies to every multi-record, state-transition, settlement or external-effecting intent.
- Model/static: one project-owned Action or published Runtime System Operation owns validation, authorization, reads, writes and terminal output. It declares complete involved objects and effect sets.
- Runtime: request and audit traces show exactly one command invocation; retries reuse the same idempotency identity.
- Blocks: partial REST choreography, multiple endpoint calls required for success, or split authorization decisions.

### G06 Atomic transaction and rollback

- Applies when one command writes more than one record/table or couples a business write with audit/outbox/receipt state.
- Model/static: read/write sets close over Handler capabilities and the contract requires one Runtime-owned unit of work. Project source cannot open or commit its own database transaction.
- Runtime: inject failure after each write boundary and before commit; all business mutations, receipt, audit and outbox state roll back together. A retry produces one complete terminal result.
- Blocks: best-effort audit/outbox, artifact-first multi-step completion without repair, or tests that assert only the success response.

### G07 Idempotency and exact fingerprinting

- Applies to every externally reachable mutation and every retryable worker/provider effect.
- Model/static: a required stable idempotency identity is declared; fingerprints use normalized exact JSON values and include semantic preconditions while excluding secrets/volatile transport values.
- Runtime: missing key is rejected, same key/same semantic payload replays the original receipt across restart, same key/different payload conflicts, concurrent duplicates execute once, and commit-unknown is reconciled.
- Blocks: invocation-ID fallback for public HTTP, float64 conversion of money/large integers, pre-normalization claim collisions, or retry generating a new key.

### G08 Concurrency, compare-and-set and fencing

- Applies to mutations of existing records, capacity/inventory/balance changes, leases and asynchronous jobs.
- Model/static: each existing-record write declares either lock-before-write (`get_for_update`) or conditional/CAS update; leases carry owner, token and expiry fencing.
- Runtime: simultaneous competing commands prove the invariant, exactly one allowed transition where required, stable conflict errors, no lost update, and stale workers cannot commit.
- Blocks: read-then-unconditional-update, unstable retry loops, fixed leases without a completion/fencing policy, or merely serial unit tests.

## C. Domain and data integrity

### G09 Exact quantities, money and ratios

- Applies to currency, money, price, cost, fee, tax, balance, points, quantities whose scale matters, rates, ratios and percentages.
- Model/static: exact named types, currency/unit, scale and rounding owner are declared. Action input/output `currency`, `decimal`, and `percent` fields reuse a named Object source field and inherit its exact contract. Project Action/domain source cannot use binary floating point or ignore parse/range errors for these values.
- Runtime: boundary, rounding, negative/zero, maximum precision, replay and aggregation cases match the frozen rule snapshot.
- Blocks: `float64` money, silently defaulting parse failures to zero, string formatting as calculation, or current Settings used to recalculate historical results.

### G10 Historical truth, snapshots and corrections

- Applies to settlement, billing, commission, payroll, inventory valuation, points or other historical results.
- Model/static: policy identity/version, input snapshot, ordered calculation trace, result and immutable ledger entries are persisted; correction is reversal/adjustment, not mutation.
- Runtime: changing current Settings does not alter old results; refund/cancel/correction appends linked entries and preserves net invariants.
- Blocks: recomputation from current configuration, editable settled facts, or missing provenance.

### G11 Database constraints and physical schema

- Applies to every durable Object/table and relation.
- Model/static: not-null, unique, foreign-key/check constraints and indexes reflect the business invariant; index definitions include ordered columns, uniqueness, direction and predicate where relevant. Reconciliation compares physical definitions, not names only.
- Runtime: migrations succeed on the current managed Runtime/database cohort from clean and upgrade states (migration definitions stay dialect-portable across supported drivers); constraint violations return stable errors without partial writes.
- Blocks: application-only uniqueness, missing tenant prefix in uniqueness/indexes, or failed introspection treated as an empty healthy state.

### G12 Audit, outbox and receipt correlation

- Applies to every mutation, workflow/job transition, external effect and privileged read/export.
- Model/static: the contract declares audit event, receipt identity, correlation chain and after-commit/outbox owner. Terminal states distinguish intent, accepted, sent, delivered, reconciled and failed.
- Runtime: request ID to invocation/action/workflow/job/outbox/provider/notification IDs is traversable; failure/restart produces one consistent terminal chain.
- Blocks: best-effort audit loss, `queued` called delivered, replay returning an artifact whose audit/download chain is incomplete, or secrets in evidence.

## D. Security and tenancy

### G13 Credentials, sessions and tokens

- Applies to authenticated deployments.
- Model/static: no fixed/default production credential; bootstrap uses invitation or cryptographically random one-time credentials with forced change/expiry. Refresh consume-and-rotate is atomic and detects reuse.
- Runtime: fresh production-like database rejects documented/default passwords; concurrent refresh permits one successor; revoke/restart/workspace mismatch and token-family reuse behave correctly.
- Blocks: hard-coded `123456`, ignored configured password policy, non-atomic refresh rotation or fail-open lockout state.

### G14 Authorization, tenant scope and row-level isolation

- Applies to multi-tenant or scoped business data.
- **Isolation is enforced at the application layer and is database-agnostic.** Tenant isolation is the `workspace_id` boundary carried by every row and applied to every query; business row scope is the declared `data_permissions` scope/predicate evaluated against actor claims. This holds identically on every supported dialect. Do NOT depend on, require, prove, or claim any database-engine feature — in particular PostgreSQL row-level security (`relrowsecurity`, `BYPASSRLS`, forced-policy catalogs, per-connection `set_config`) — for isolation; the framework must stay portable across databases, so engine-level RLS posture is never a required capability, evidence kind, or `done` precondition.
- Model/static: least-privilege role and data scope are explicit; every scoped Object has a declared `data_permissions` entry and no scope relies on a database-engine policy.
- Runtime: at least two workspaces and differentiated actors with non-empty colliding data prove allowed access and cross-tenant/cross-scope denial through ordinary HTTP, Action, Report, export, worker and direct-query probes on the current managed Runtime database cohort.
- Blocks: empty-result tests passed off as isolation proof, role-header simulation, or any requirement for engine-specific RLS catalogs/posture as evidence.

### G15 Field security and assurance

- Applies to sensitive fields, high-risk Actions, exports or approval ceremonies.
- Model/static: read/mask/hide/write/export policy and Action output lineage are declared; enhanced assurance has a real issuer and binds workspace, user, Action, record, version and payload digest.
- Runtime: non-empty distinguishable sensitive values remain protected across Record, Action record/output, Report and export; missing/expired/replayed/mismatched assurance causes no mutation.
- Blocks: Action output bypassing field policy, empty sensitive fixtures, frontend-only approval, or `normal_login` used as enhanced assurance.

### G16 Hostile input, files, SQL, connectors and Agent tools

- Applies when the capability accepts files, URLs, Object SQL, connector input or anonymous/task capabilities.
- Model/static: parser-safe allowlists, size/type limits, clean-file receipts, SSRF/DNS/redirect rules and signed single-use Agent tool capabilities are explicit.
- Runtime: traversal/symlink/MIME deception, quarantine/scan failure, SQL CTE/subquery/UNION/comment/timeout, private/loopback/link-local/IPv6/DNS-rebinding URLs, and forged/cross-tenant/replayed Agent tool calls fail closed.
- Blocks: regex-only SQL rewriting, raw storage access, anonymous exception without negative proof, or emulator evidence presented as provider security.

## E. Query and resource performance

### G17 Execution-level bounded pagination

- Applies to every list/report/search with data-dependent cardinality.
- Model/static: API declares page size, opaque cursor, stable order and count semantics. Repository/executor accepts page/cursor and pushes `LIMIT page_size+1` or equivalent keyset/aggregate paging to the data owner. A result `limit` is only an output cap, not pagination proof.
- Runtime: first/middle/last pages at target volume show bounded rows read, query count, latency and peak memory; no full materialization precedes slicing.
- Blocks: fixed first 200/1000 rows, an Action `List` call without an explicit bounded page, full Summary followed by `paginate`, OFFSET traversal without a hard result bound plus a query-profile budget captured on the current managed Runtime database cohort, or async worker re-running the full Report for every page.

### G18 Stable traversal under change

- Applies to mutable paginated datasets.
- Model/static: every sort appends a unique deterministic tie-breaker and fixes null/collation behavior. The signed cursor either encodes the complete keyset tuple or binds an authorized source-version snapshot to a bounded offset; the latter must reject continuation after source drift.
- Runtime: equal sort keys plus concurrent insert/update/delete produce no duplicate or missing rows within the documented snapshot semantics; a source-version-fenced traversal returns a stable stale-cursor conflict rather than mixed-version rows, and retrying an unchanged cursor is deterministic.
- Blocks: custom row sort without an ID/unique tie-breaker, grouped sort without every grouping tie term, page-number-only traversal, unsigned response index, or offset continuation after source drift.

### G19 Index, query-plan and N+1 budget

- Applies to growth-sensitive reads, imports, exports, principal construction and relation resolution.
- Model/static: queries declare access pattern and expected composite/search index; loop-contained I/O requires a bounded exemption or batch interface.
- Runtime: the acceptance database uses its driver-equivalent structured plan (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for SQLite, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` for MySQL, `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)` for PostgreSQL) and binds that plan format/dialect to the managed process receipt. Machine-checked access classification confirms index-driven execution on growth-sensitive paths; SQL statement/row-count observation at 1/10/100/1000 scale stays within rows-read and query-count budgets. Small-table full scans are accepted only when the bounded dataset fits one page and the plan records that scan explicitly.
- Blocks: index-name-only checks, B-tree claimed for `%substring%`, per-membership/profile/row queries, or latency logs without thresholds.

### G20 Timeouts, capacity, memory, streaming and fairness

- Applies to external I/O, database work, workers, imports/exports and multi-tenant shared resources.
- Model/static: request/job deadlines, byte/row/CPU/attempt/concurrency limits, cancellation, streaming/chunk ownership and per-tenant fairness semantics are declared.
- Runtime: slow SQL/provider/worker cancellation stops downstream work, returns the connection/lease, prevents late writes, bounds RSS and keeps a cold tenant progressing beside a hot tenant.
- Blocks: context timeout not propagated to DB, full artifact reassembly, process-local limits called tenant-global, missing job deadline, or unbounded goroutines.

## F. Asynchronous and external lifecycle

### G21 Workflow, scheduler and automation terminal semantics

- Applies when those resources are modeled or used by a journey.
- Model/static: triggers, branches, retries, dead letters, missed-window policy, run-as identity, before/after transaction boundary and terminal states are complete.
- Runtime: process/node/task/action effects and audit all terminate correctly across retry, cancellation, permission drift and restart; before failure rolls back and after-commit work is durable.
- Blocks: HTTP enqueue alone, waiting state called success, or schedule receipt not linked to Workflow/Action effect.

### G22 Connector and provider effect reconciliation

- Applies to any external provider call.
- Model/static: connection/provider identity, operation DTOs, timeout/retry safety, idempotency, outbox, response reference, callback/reconciliation and compensation are declared.
- Runtime: real configured provider evidence proves effect and reconciliation; retry/restart does not duplicate it, and uncertain outcomes remain explicitly reconcilable.
- Blocks: deterministic emulator as provider acceptance, SMTP accepted as delivered, or synchronous external call while holding database locks.

### G23 Worker lease, deadline and restart recovery

- Applies to asynchronous jobs, exports/imports, report workers, Agent tasks and background reconciliation.
- Model/static: durable queue, bounded claim, heartbeat, fencing token, deadline, attempts, terminal/dead-letter state and cleanup SLA exist.
- Runtime: kill the old PID during each critical window, prove a new PID with the same database/delivery recovers once, stale owner cannot commit, and no item is lost or duplicated.
- Blocks: in-memory queue, PID-less restart evidence, lease without fencing, or a worker test double.

### G24 Notification and after-commit delivery

- Applies when user/system notification is part of the accepted journey.
- Model/static: event identity, audience, template, durable inbox/outbox state, channel semantics and retry policy are bound to the owning terminal business event.
- Runtime: after commit/restart/replay, Inbox and channel effects appear once with correct actor/workspace visibility; rollback produces none.
- Blocks: direct pre-commit send, duplicate terminal notification, template-only evidence, or channel failure hidden by Inbox success.

## G. SSE and Agent lifecycle

### G25 SSE identity, resume and durable refetch

- Applies to every disclosed stream.
- Model/static: event type, stable event ID, cursor/`Last-Event-ID`, retention/resync contract, authorization and durable refetch endpoint are published. Invalidation is not durable data.
- Runtime: disconnect after a known event, reconnect with cursor, cover retained and expired cursors, restart and slow consumer; refetch returns the durable terminal truth without missing or duplicating effects.
- Blocks: accepted/result events without IDs, client with no reconnect path, connect-only tests, or process memory presented as durable replay.

### G26 Agent authorization and provider identity

- Applies when Agent/agent-task capability is claimed.
- Model/static: allowed tools/effect sets, service principal, workspace/role/scope recovery, provider configuration, model/policy and anonymous capability exceptions are explicit.
- Runtime: a real configured provider returns external run/model/usage identity; forged/escalated/cross-workspace tools are denied and source handlers remain inside frozen capabilities.
- Blocks: deterministic response fixture as Agent acceptance, bearer role simulation, or generic tool proxy.

### G27 Agent retry, cancellation, reconciliation and receipts

- Applies to asynchronous or tool-using Agent runs.
- Model/static: task/run/tool-call identities, lease/fencing, retry safety, cancel semantics, partial tool effects and reconciliation are declared.
- Runtime: cancel/retry/worker loss/provider timeout/restart produce one terminal task, durable tool receipts and reconciled business effects.
- Blocks: UI cancellation only, retry creating a new uncontrolled task, or final text without tool/effect receipts.

### G28 Multi-instance event/session durability

- Applies when more than one Runtime replica or failover is claimed.
- Model/static: session, rate limit, event backplane, cursor and worker coordination owners are shared or explicitly instance-local with limited claims.
- Runtime: requests/retries/streams cross replicas, one replica dies, and authorization, limits, fan-out, resume and work ownership remain correct.
- Blocks: process-local backplane/limiter advertised as global, sticky-session assumption without contract, or single-instance evidence used for HA.

## H. Operations and acceptance integrity

### G29 Observability, redaction and alert recovery

- Applies to production deployment.
- Model/static: low-cardinality metrics, structured logs, trace/correlation fields, redaction policy, queue/worker/provider/database indicators and actionable alerts are defined.
- Runtime: success and injected failure show the complete correlation chain; secrets are absent; lag/retry/dead-letter/capacity alerts fire and recover.
- Blocks: dashboard JSON or metric name existence alone, rows iteration omitted from SQL timing, or unbounded tenant/user labels.

### G30 Failure-window and commit-unknown injection

- Applies to every multi-step durable or external-effect lifecycle.
- Model/static: critical windows are enumerated: before write, between writes, before/after commit acknowledgement, before/after outbox/provider callback, receipt/audit finalization and restart.
- Runtime: deterministic failpoints cover each applicable window; retry/reconcile reaches one legal terminal state without partial invisible effects.
- Blocks: success-only tests, rollback tested only before the first write, or commit-unknown treated as a generic internal error.

### G31 Target dialect, migration, backup and upgrade recovery

- Applies to the current managed Runtime database cohort and the upgrade paths claimed by the release; code and migrations remain dialect-portable across the supported sqlite/mysql/postgres drivers (see G14), while runtime acceptance evidence is captured only on that cohort's driver.
- Model/static: compatibility matrix, migration order, lock/statement timeouts, rollback/forward-fix, backup/restore and retention/partition strategy are versioned.
- Runtime: clean install, previous-version upgrade, interrupted migration, backup restore and Runtime restart pass on the managed cohort with current roles.
- Blocks: an ephemeral/non-durable database target (for SQLite, `:memory:` cannot prove restart or backup-restore), ignored introspection error, source tests without packaged migration execution, a second profiling engine, or evidence whose dialect differs from the managed cohort. Portability note: no evidence may rest on an engine-proprietary feature as a cross-driver product invariant; multi-dialect runtime evidence is not required for one project cohort.

### G32 Typed evidence, exact denominator and anti-self-report

- Applies to every terminal acceptance claim.
- Model/static: each case requires typed observation schemas whose validators parse behavior facts, not only files and hashes. Denominator generation is exact-set, resource-closed and capability-specific; evidence producer and identities are bound.
- Runtime: checker independently verifies HTTP status/route/error, transaction/readback, cursor/query profile, old/new PID and DB identity, worker/provider terminal state, differentiated data-scope isolation and correlation facts.

# Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract; frontend dependency installation and package wiring are outside this Skill.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, BFF, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. Application-facing client selection and wiring belong to the frontend owner outside this Skill; Builder models only the Application Delivery-published `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}/run`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/records/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Backend acceptance wraps typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, Product Surface, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request (gate: G04). For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

For normal whole-project work, start and inspect the Runtime through separate managed Runtime start/status Gates in the current Host/Agent session TODO, using the packaged CLI, current project-relative bundle, and an explicit numeric loopback address such as `127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. The Gate runner validates the exact argv and source/Runtime/cohort bindings and requires the `domainry-managed-runtime-process-v3` response/receipt. A failed start or status Gate remains immutable evidence: diagnose it, repair the owner, append a uniquely labeled repair-round Gate pair to the same TODO, sync, rerun, and continue. Neither Gate closes the broader acceptance-session and differentiated-data readiness item.

Use the machine-owned `runtime-process-continuation` profile only for a caller-explicit standalone recovery after an earlier Agent task has ended. Its compact TODO and returned recipes are not the normal whole-project phase transition. Stop with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project <project>` after acceptance. The managed receipt records the address, so subsequent acceptance commands use the same Runtime cohort. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or assemble Runtime Gate controls by hand.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Stop Runtime and reclaim ports and processes after scenarios. A running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These idioms come from real Handler defects observed at runtime; `project source finalize`, compile, tests, and `project check` do NOT catch any of them.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Unlike the idioms below, `project source finalize` DOES reject the following three contracts (`backend_technical_contract` check), so each violation costs a failed-finalize round-trip — one real run hit 8 violations at once. Check every Handler before finalizing: (1) no generated capability I/O inside any loop (`for`/`range`) or recursive call cycle — do pure selection into bounded slices and call the generated batch/query capability once outside the loop; (2) every List query declares `Page(page, pageSize)` with a literal page size from 1 through 200 — an unpaged first result is forbidden; (3) no discarded call result or error — assign every capability return and handle every error. Generated batch inputs are 1 through 200, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal accepted fan-out shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's own `project verify` supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** A `conditional_update` Handler mutation without a compare-and-set token or predicate fails at runtime with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. Attach the condition observed under `GetForUpdate`:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)` predicates and `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)` are the generated condition surface (arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects are inherently compare-and-set and also satisfy the requirement). On idempotent replay the predicate legitimately differs (equal-to-current instead of null); test assertions must compare per-execution expected mutations, not demand identical mutations.

The generated data package exports `ValidateConditionalMutation`, and both the real data layer and the scaffolded fakes enforce it — a mutation with no condition fails unit tests with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. A hand-written fake must route through the same helper; never write one that accepts an unconditional mutation. As a cheap belt-and-suspenders guard for call sites no unit case exercises, after implementing each module and before `project source finalize`, run the static self-check from the project root and require exit code 0 (`grep -L` alone does not encode the verdict in its exit status, so the wrapper below is the command to bind as Gate evidence):

```bash
bash -c 'viol=$(grep -rl --include="*.go" -e ".ConditionalUpdate(" backend | grep -v "/generated/" | grep -v "_test\.go" | xargs -r grep -LE "Require[A-Za-z]+\(|WithExpectedUpdatedAt\(|Increment[A-Za-z]*\(|Decrement[A-Za-z]*\("); [ -z "$viol" ] || { echo "$viol"; exit 1; }'
```

Exit 1 lists every file that builds a `ConditionalUpdate` with no condition anywhere in that file; each will fail live with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. The check is file-granular: a file that mixes one conditioned and one bare call still passes, so keep one handler per file (the default layout). The development TODO template carries this as a required implementation-stage checkbox — bind it with `... run <gate-id> --bind source --` followed by the command above verbatim (it already starts with `bash -c`).

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.
